qualifying_findings.title: GhostSplice shows malicious MCP servers can split instructions across trusted agent channels

visible_dates.basis: primary research page month only; outside exact cutoff, retained as supporting technical source

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: The Hacker News reported ASSET Research Group's GhostSplice technique: a malicious MCP server can place separately harmless-looking instruction fragments in tool descriptions, tool results, and sampling channels so a coding agent combines them and exfiltrates SSH keys, .env secrets, source code, or customer data. The report notes controlled tests with fake credentials and no CVE identifiers as of August 10, 2026.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reputable security news with primary research support; controlled proof-of-concept, not confirmed in-the-wild intrusion
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MCP-connected coding agents that already trust a malicious or compromised MCP server and can read the targeted files.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It turns MCP server trust into an agent-context supply-chain problem: instruction boundaries at the protocol level do not guarantee that the agent will keep tool metadata and results from recombining into a malicious objective.

upstream_routing.local_security_implication: Agent and tool security, MCP server trust, prompt injection, and secret exfiltration controls belong in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Broad MCP protocol and MCP server catalog context belongs upstream in ai-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General coding-agent workflow and MCP adoption guidance belongs upstream in ai-dev-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the in-window secondary report; medium confidence on precise primary publication date because the research page exposes only July 2026 in fetched content.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare against existing MCP trust, prompt-injection, and coding-agent command-boundary leaves.
Check whether ASSET or affected clients publish coordinated CVEs or vendor mitigations after the report.

qualifying_findings.title: Ghostjacking uses poisoned logs and alerts to hijack AI agents through trusted operational tools
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: SecurityWeek reported Tenet's DEF CON Ghostjacking demonstration, where malicious instructions are planted in logs or alerts that an AI agent later reviews. Reported cases targeted Cloudflare logs, Datadog alerts, and Sentry-to-coding-agent handoffs; the article says tests caused DNS changes, code execution, and cloud credential or environment secret exfiltration in controlled demonstrations.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reputable security news covering vendor research demonstration
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Agent workflows that let one AI read operational logs, alerts, or AI-generated fixes and then act through Cloudflare, Datadog, Sentry, build systems, Kubernetes, or similar trusted operational tools.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It shows that blocked malicious input can remain dangerous when faithfully logged and later consumed by an authorized agent with action privileges.

upstream_routing.local_security_implication: Operational log trust boundaries, agent action authorization, and cross-agent trust chains belong in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Broad product pages for Cloudflare, Datadog, Sentry, and Claude belong upstream in ai-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General coding-agent incident workflow practices belong upstream in ai-dev-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the article date and technical summary; primary Tenet page should be fetched during ingest for exact vendor wording if accessible.
follow_up_actions: Route to agent-and-tool-security and incident-response leaves covering log ingestion, delegated authority, and cross-agent trust.
Look for vendor advisories or configuration mitigations from Cloudflare, Datadog, Sentry, Anthropic, or Tenet.

qualifying_findings.title: Cursor advisories describe macOS Auto-Run Sandbox escapes through Python virtual environments and Docker

visible_dates.basis: GitHub advisory publication date; outside cutoff but primary patch context

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-73217 says Cursor IDE before 3.1.2 on macOS lets an agent in Auto-Run Sandbox mode replace a virtual environment Python executable; the Microsoft Python extension can later invoke it outside the sandbox, allowing host commands with user privileges. CVE-2026-73218, visible in Tenable's updated CVE feed on August 11, describes a pre-3.0.0 Cursor sandbox escape involving Docker Desktop and Dev Containers that can mount Docker's virtiofs0 and gain home-directory read/write and host command execution without an additional prompt.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability advisory and vulnerability database update
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Cursor IDE for macOS before 3.1.2 for CVE-2026-73217 and before 3.0.0 for CVE-2026-73218.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The findings test the core assumption that an autonomous coding agent's sandbox prevents host-side file modification and command execution when the agent can mutate developer environment artifacts.

upstream_routing.local_security_implication: Coding-agent sandbox escapes, host command boundaries, and patch requirements belong in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Cursor as a developer-tool entity belongs upstream in ai-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General Cursor usage and coding-agent workflow guidance belongs upstream in ai-dev-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE-2026-73217 because the GitHub advisory and Vulners timeline agree. Medium-high for CVE-2026-73218 because the visible source was a live CVE feed rather than a fetched GHSA detail page.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, split CVE-2026-73217 and CVE-2026-73218 if they need independent leaves.
Check NVD and Cursor advisories for CVE-2026-73218 canonical GHSA details before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: Claude Code Templates Studio vulnerability exposes unauthenticated command execution from a local agent tool server

visible_dates.basis: project changelog patch date; outside cutoff but primary fix context

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-73222 describes Claude Code Templates before 1.29.4 launching Claude Code Studio on all interfaces at port 3444 with permissive CORS and no authentication. Request fields reached child_process.spawn with shell execution enabled, enabling an attacker who can reach the port or lure a developer to a malicious page to run OS commands with developer privileges; the changelog says 1.29.4 removed shell execution, constrained arguments, bound to loopback, and restricted CORS.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database update with project changelog patch evidence
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: claude-code-templates prior to 1.29.4 when Claude Code Studio is launched with --studio.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent companion tools can become high-privilege local control planes; unauthenticated local studio surfaces need the same origin, authentication, and shell-injection controls as any developer service.

upstream_routing.local_security_implication: Local agent tool server exposure, command execution, and developer credential compromise belong in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Claude Code Templates as a developer-tool entity belongs upstream in ai-wiki if cataloged.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General Claude Code workflow and local tool setup guidance belongs upstream in ai-dev-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the vulnerability content and fix because the project changelog matches the CVE summary; in-window qualification relies on the August 11 CVE publication/update.
follow_up_actions: Check the GHSA page directly during ingest if accessible.

qualifying_findings.title: DB-GPT v0.8.1 path traversal advisory enables arbitrary file write and possible RCE

visible_dates.basis: NVD published and last modified dates

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published CVE-2026-73034 for DB-GPT v0.8.1: an unauthenticated remote attacker can inject directory traversal sequences into the user_id HTTP header of the Python file-upload endpoint, write arbitrary files outside the intended directory, and potentially reach remote code execution through Python startup hooks, cron directories, or agent scripts.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD and CVE record for AI application vulnerability
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: DB-GPT v0.8.1, affected through at least 0.8.1 per NVD affected range.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is an AI application/runtime platform vulnerability where upload trust boundaries can become code execution against deployed AI/agent infrastructure.

upstream_routing.local_security_implication: AI runtime/file-upload boundary and deployment hardening belong in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: DB-GPT as an AI application/framework entity belongs upstream in ai-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General DB-GPT development use belongs upstream in ai-dev-wiki only if it affects AI-assisted development practice.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence because NVD exposes the change history and CVE description inside the in-window publication date.
follow_up_actions: Check DB-GPT issue and commit before ingesting mitigation details.

qualifying_findings.title: PapersGPT for Zotero RCE advisory links prompt injection and malicious LLM responses to Zotero privilege

visible_dates.basis: CVE record publication visible in search result

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-73032 describes PapersGPT for Zotero 0.6.1 executing arbitrary JavaScript when a malicious LLM endpoint, MITM, or prompt-injected PDF returns code that is passed unsanitized to window.eval() in views.ts. The advisory says execution occurs in Zotero's chrome-privileged context, enabling file read/write, process execution, and access to Zotero data.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE record and vulnerability database update
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is a concrete prompt-injection-to-code-execution path in an AI-assisted document/research workflow, where model output crosses directly into privileged local extension execution.

upstream_routing.local_security_implication: Prompt injection, unsafe model-output handling, and privileged plugin execution belong in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: PapersGPT and model-provider catalog context belongs upstream in ai-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General research-agent or document workflow practice belongs upstream in ai-dev-wiki if treated as an AI-assisted work pattern.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence: CVE publication is visible and corroborated by a vulnerability listing, but NVD detail was not fetched successfully in this run.

qualifying_findings.title: Netskope reports relisted AI Sidebar Chrome extension shipping new malicious updates after prior AI-chat theft
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Netskope reported that the Chrome extension 'AI Sidebar with DeepSeek AI' had previously been removed for scraping ChatGPT and DeepSeek conversations, then reappeared and delivered updates through Google's CRX CDN to enterprise endpoints. Version 1.7.3.0 added a 21-line malicious monetization payload that opens affiliate links on update and uninstall; Netskope classifies the CRX as Trojan.GenericFCA.Script.37952 and recommends removing extension ID inhcgfpbfdjbjogdfjbclgolkmhnooop.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary threat research with indicators of compromise, corroborated by security news
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Chrome extension ID inhcgfpbfdjbjogdfjbclgolkmhnooop; malicious version 1.7.3.0; prior pre-1.7.x builds exfiltrated AI conversation content.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It shows AI-chat browser extensions as a data-security and supply-chain boundary: marketplace relisting and auto-update channels can reintroduce code to managed browsers after prior conversation theft.

upstream_routing.local_security_implication: AI conversation theft, browser extension supply chain, enterprise browser controls, and data exfiltration belong in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki_note: Broad product/provider pages for ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Chrome, Aitopia, and browser-extension products belong upstream in ai-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki_note: General browser-extension governance for development workflows belongs upstream in ai-dev-wiki only when framed as practice guidance.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence because the primary source has an in-window date, concrete version numbers, IOC hashes/domains, and mitigation guidance.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, avoid duplicating broad ChatGPT or DeepSeek pages; keep the local leaf focused on extension-mediated AI conversation theft and browser supply-chain controls.
Check Chrome Web Store status and any Google response before publication.
